USAGE:
    dotnet pubwiz [path] [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

ARGUMENTS:
    [path]    Folder, solution (.sln/.slnx) or project (.csproj) to publish.    
              Defaults to the current folder                                    

OPTIONS:
                                DEFAULT                                         
    -h, --help                             Prints help information              
    -v, --version                          Prints version information           
    -c, --configuration                    Build configuration, overriding the  
                                           profiles' (e.g. Release or Debug)    
        --os <OS>                          The OS to build for when the target  
                                           doesn't decide it (folders, zips,    
                                           FTP, SFTP): win, linux or osx. Add   
                                           the architecture to set both, e.g.   
                                           linux-arm64. Default: this machine's;
                                           IIS builds for Windows, Azure apps   
                                           and containers for theirs            
    -a, --arch <ARCH>                      The architecture to build for: x64,  
                                           arm64, x86 or arm. Default: x64 for  
                                           servers, Azure and other OSes; this  
                                           machine's for its own OS             
        --preset <NAME>                    Run a saved preset from pubwiz.json  
                                           instead of the wizard                
        --preset-file <FILE>               The preset file to use (default:     
                                           pubwiz.json in the folder or its     
                                           parents)                             
        --project <NAME>                   Publish this project (name or .csproj

result.stdout:
DESCRIPTION:
Write a transformed web.config (same transforms as publishing) without 
publishing

USAGE:
    dotnet pubwiz transform [path] [OPTIONS]

ARGUMENTS:
    [path]    Folder, solution or project containing the web.config. Defaults to
              the current folder                                                

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help                Prints help information                           
    -c, --configuration       Applies web.<configuration>.config (asked for when
                              omitted)                                          
    -p, --profile             Applies web.<profile>.config and                  
                              Properties/PublishProfiles/<profile>.transform    
    -e, --environment         Applies web.<environment>.config                  
    -t, --transform <FILE>    An extra transform file to apply last (repeatable)
    -o, --output <FILE>       Where to write the result. Defaults to            
                              obj/pubwiz/transformed/web.config in the project  
        --print               Also print the transformed file

DESCRIPTION:
Save logins per server; they replace the user and password of Web Deploy, FTP 
and SFTP profiles for that server

USAGE:
    dotnet pubwiz servers [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help    Prints help information

COMMANDS:
    set <server>       Save the user name and password for a server
    list               Show the servers with a saved login         
    remove <server>    Forget a server's login

DESCRIPTION:
Save the user name and password for a server

USAGE:
    dotnet pubwiz servers set <server> [OPTIONS]

ARGUMENTS:
    <server>    The server as written in profiles: an IP address or name (a port
                or URL is fine too)                                             

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help              Prints help information                             
    -u, --user <NAME>       The user to sign in as (asked for when missing)     
        --password-stdin    Read the password from standard input instead of    
                            asking, e.g. in setup scripts
